Chess pieces:

- The pawn moves to one field forward or two fields at the first move of this figure; beats diagonally to one field forward.
- The king moves to one field in the vertical, horizontal or diagonal.
- The queen moves to any distance vertically, horizontally or diagonally.
- The rook moves to any distance vertically or horizontally.
- The knight moves to the field two fields along the vertical and one horizontally or one field vertically and two horizontally.
- The bishop moves to any distance diagonally.

Important Chess situations:

- Check - the situation in chess when a king is under immediate attack by opponent's pieces
- Checkmate - the situation in chess when the player whose turn it is to move is in check and has no legal move to escape check.
- Stalemate - the situation in chess when the player whose turn it is to move has no legal move and is not in check. (draw)

The goal of the game is to checkmate the other king.

Two special moves in Chess:

- Castling is a double move, performed by the king and the rook that never moved.
- En passant is a move in which a pawn can take an opponent's pawn if it jumps over a field under the pawn's blow.

Okey is a traditional tile-based game with long history and many variations. It's highly popular in Turkey among Turkish people, played mainly in coffee houses by people in every age. It's very similar to Rummy / Rummikub as it is played with the same set of boards and tiles but with different rules.

Realistic feeling, simple interface, and exciting gameplay!

Okey Game is played by four players with a set of 106 tiles, and 104 of them are numbered from 1 to 13 with four different colors. During the game, each player has 14 tiles on their board. On each turn, a player draws one tile and discards one tile. The goal of the game is to be first to form a board that consists of sets and runs using all 14 tiles. There are special tiles chosen in every game, called jokers, which help the player form his 14 tiles board of sets and runs by replacing the missing tile. The last two tiles from the 106-tile-set represented with stars are tricky 'false jokers', which against expectations, act as normal numbered tiles.

Features:
● Advanced Artificial Intelligence.
● Full HD graphics (perfect for high-resolution tablets).
● Unlimited hours of joy.
● Multiple game modes.
● High playability.
● High-quality animations.

You can tap and hold a tile in the same place for 3 seconds to flip it. This is generally used as a reminder of joker tiles in Okey game.

-King: Moves 1 square in any direction (key to protect—losing it means checkmate!).
-Queen: Moves any number of squares horizontally, vertically, or diagonally (most powerful piece).

Callbreak turns a 13-card hand into a prediction. Before the first card is played, you decide how many tricks the hand should win. That bid becomes the standard for every choice that follows: when to take control, when to stay patient, and when a saved trump is worth more than an immediate win.

The decision loop

1. Read the hand. Look at high cards, long suits, weak suits, and the spades that may give you control later.
2. Bid for tricks. Set a target that reflects the whole hand rather than one attractive card.
3. Track the lead suit. Follow it whenever possible and notice which players stop having that suit.
4. Manage spades as trump. Use them when you cannot follow suit, but keep enough flexibility for the closing tricks.
5. Check the result. Meeting your bid supports your score; missing it turns an ambitious prediction into a setback.

This trick-taking game uses all 52 cards, with 13 cards dealt to each player. The rules are easy to begin learning, but the choices stay interesting because information changes after every play. A card that looked safe at the start may become more important once a suit is exhausted. A conservative bid may protect a difficult hand, while an aggressive bid asks for better timing from the first lead onward.

Imposter Up - Who is the Spy? is a fun party game of hidden roles, bluffing, and social deduction. Whether you're on a video call, hanging out with friends, or hosting a game night, this spy-themed experience brings laughter, tension, and strategy to every group.

In each round, players receive the same secret word, except one: the Imposter. Their mission is to fake it, blend in, and guess the word without getting caught. The Civilians must subtly confirm each other’s knowledge while staying alert for suspicious behavior.

But there’s a twist: one player is Mr. White. They get no word at all. No hints, no help. Just pure bluffing! If Mr White survives or guesses the word, they win the round.

How it works:

◆ Ask indirect questions and give vague answers
◆ Listen closely for hesitation, slip-ups, or overconfidence
◆ Vote to eliminate the most suspicious player
◆ One by one, players are voted out until the truth is revealed

Each game is quick, intense, and totally unpredictable. Whether you're the Imposter, Mr. White, or a Civilian, your goal is to deceive or detect—and survive the round.

Key Features:

◆ Play with 3 to 24 players - ideal for small groups or large parties
◆ Choose from Imposter, Mr. White, and Civilian roles
◆ Simple to learn, full of strategy and replayability
◆ Includes hundreds of secret words and themed word packs
◆ Designed for friends and family parties, remote play, or even casual calls
◆ Fast-paced rounds that keep everyone engaged

If you enjoy spy games, party games, or hidden identity challenges, you'll love the twist that Imposter Up - Who is the Spy? brings to the table.

Download now and put your social skills to the test. Will you blend in, uncover the truth, or get voted out first?

 How to play Ludo 

Ludo Match starts with a fixed number of tokens for each player in their starting box, which are then moved around the board by rolling the dice on their turn. Players must roll a six to place their token at the starting position. The first player to get all of their tokens inside the HOME wins the game. The game can get competitive, with players sending each other fun emotes and trying to outsmart each other on the board.

 Ludo Match rules 

 - A token can start to move only if the dice rolled is a 6.
 - Each player gets a turn wise chance to roll the dice. And if the player rolls a 6, they will get another chance to roll the dice again.
 - All the tokens must reach the center of the board to win the game.
 - The token move clockwise according to the number of rolled dice.
 - Knocking out other's tokens will give you an extra chance to roll the dice again.

Jam Bus: Sandfall brings a fresh twist to bus jam, color puzzle, and traffic escape gameplay.
Colorful sand is stacked in layers, and every bus has its own color and direction. Tap the right bus, collect the matching sand, and clear the board step by step. Sounds simple at first, but every move can change the whole puzzle.
Plan carefully before you tap. Some buses may block each other. Some paths may cross. Some sand colors can only be cleared after the lower layers are gone. To win, you need to observe the board, choose the right order, and keep every bus moving without a crash.
How to play
• Tap a bus to move it along its route
 • Match each bus with the same color sand
 • Clear lower sand layers to unlock the ones above
 • Avoid traffic crashes when paths cross
 • Solve each level with smart sequencing
Why you’ll enjoy Jam Bus: Sandfall
• Easy tap controls
 • Relaxing color-matching gameplay
 • Clever bus parking jam puzzles
 • Satisfying sand-clearing effects
 • Increasingly tricky routes and layers
 • Clean visuals and smooth puzzle flow
 • Great for quick breaks and brain training
Every level is a small logic challenge. A bus may look ready to move, but its route might block another vehicle. A color may be visible, but the sand below it must be cleared first. Think ahead, follow the arrows, and find the perfect order to clear the whole sandfall.
If you enjoy bus games, parking jam puzzles, color sort games, traffic escape challenges, or relaxing logic games, Jam Bus: Sandfall gives you a colorful new puzzle to solve.
Start with one bus, clear one color, and let the sand fall into place.

- You and your opponent receive 7 tiles with letters on them from a tile bag. You have to connect letters in different ways and place the tiles on the board to make a word.
- Words can be formed either horizontally or vertically, much like in crosswords.
- The player who starts the word game should place a word containing at least two letters onto the board with at least one tile placed in the central square.
- There are 44 bonus cells on the board. They allow you to multiply the points you receive either for a letter or the whole word if a tile with a letter is placed on one of them.
- If you receive a tile with a joker, lucky you! It can substitute any letter you need while playing word puzzle games.
- The game is over when either player uses the last tile, or both of them skip two moves in a row, or if either player has no possible moves left. Also, it is possible to resign from the word game. However, this means that your opponent wins.
- The user with the higher score at the end of the game wins.

- Word definition. The built-in dictionary provides the definition of all the words added onto the board. This is an excellent opportunity to enrich your vocabular
